utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Could the registrar call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-11-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milan Martic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Can you hear me? I cannot hear you. Okay, let's try to go ahead. Can we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Your Honour. Alex Whiting -- Alex Whiting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Along with Ms. Sabine Bauer and Ms. Lakshmie Walpita, case manager, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: My apologies. Once again, good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Predrag Milovancevic. I'm an attorney from Belgrade. I am representing the accused Martic. Next to me is my assistant, Vuk Sekulic, attorney from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Mr. Martic, please. Can you hear the proceedings, what we are going to be saying here -- stand up, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Can you hear the proceedings in a language you can understand perfectly well?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: You may sit down, please. Well, I am informed about what has been going on so far on this case, and I say that in addressing you about several aspects of the case to be dealt with at present. I am confident that it is working pretty well. First of all, I understand that the disclosure procedures are going at a good pace and that you are not having so much problem with that. Also, that you are also making contacts between the parties - can you hear me well? - between the parties about the possibility of some agreements of facts, which seems to be very interesting to us to know. Also, I want to tell you and to emphasise that the Chamber is very interested and would be most helping with whatever you may ask about the protection of witnesses. Not only for the Prosecution, but I had understood that also for the Defence this may be a problem, and we are ready to try to solve whatever your problems may be. And finally, I would like to thank you also, because you are working at a pace that even if we are not going to be able to start the hearing of the case in October, as was previously suggested in the previous Status Conference, I am glad that -- and I am confident that probably in very short delay you will be ready to start. So that is what I have been told so far. I want to take this moment to ask you, the Prosecution and the counsel for the accused, to state to me and suggest to me whatever problems you may have in connection with the case. So please, the Prosecutor, would you like to add, to explain some problem or issue you would like to mention here?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I wouldn't say that we're having any problems with the case. As the Court has stated, things are moving along at a good pace. Disclosure is proceeding. Of course it's an ongoing process, particularly with respect to Rule 68 as we continue to review the material and provide it to the Defence and have a dialogue with the Defence so that we can more specifically identify what it is that they need and also make it clear to them what we have reviewed. So that, I think, dialogue is beginning and is productive. With respect to the efforts on agreement of facts, the Court is right that there has been contact. A process has started. To be candid, I don't think we have made tremendous progress so far in reaching agreement, but I'm very hopeful, based on our most recent discussions, that with some additional time we will be able to make progress as both sides focus a little bit more and as the Defence has more of an opportunity to review the material that's being provided to them, I think that we can - and I certainly hope - that we can narrow the issues for trial. But that is obviously a process that will require a little bit more time and it may be something that we seek assistance from the senior legal officer in trying to negotiate that. As we told the senior legal officer on Friday, we will be filing a protective measures motion within the next two or three weeks with respect to perhaps ten or so witness. So as the Court noted, we don't -- we're not ready in October, but the delay, I think, will be productive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you. What about you, the counsel for the accused? Do you have any suggestion or issue to raise at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the Defence is concerned, Your Honour, we could say right now that the Defence agrees what -- with what the colleague Prosecutor just told you. We do have communication. The disclosure of material under Rule 68 is currently in progress. What is important both for us, for the Court, and for the colleagues from the Prosecution is that this material is voluminous. So far we have received 4.000 of potential exculpatory material under Rule 68. Naturally, the Defence is not mandated to read the entire material, but just to review it, to select relevant portions, and to proceed to work on it. So this procedure is currently in progress. What is also very important for the Defence is that the Prosecution maintains that rhythm so that on one hand the Defence is not overburdened with material and on the other hand so that we have an opportunity to review the material because we have undertaken that as our obligation with respect to the Court, to review the material using our own resources. We have received an offer from the Prosecution pertaining to 45 items. We responded to all of those points, and last Friday we received Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the opinion of the Prosecution concerning the offer. On one hand, we are discussing the so-called general issues, and it probably would be the best if the Prosecution and the Defence could agree on that. But taking into account the relevant period of the indictment, the territory to which the criminal enterprise pertains, I can tell you that this is a very delicate issue, and we expect that, with the assistance of Mr. Harhoff and in contacts with the Prosecution, we should be able to agree on all of the issues that are possible right now at this stage in the proceedings. Naturally, we need to agree on certain legal and factual issues that are not part of the merits of the case. I hope that we will be successful in this. Right now, we don't have any other issues to bring up, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you. I am very happy to know that you are in the right way, if I may say so. So I will turn now to Mr. Martic -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon, Your Honour. The record states 4.000 pages. I have to correct it. It is not 4.000 but, rather, 400.000 pages that we need to review. So could this please be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Yes. It doesn't mean that it puts you with a problem you cannot deal with. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: It's incorrect, imprecise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's all I wanted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milovancevic. So I turn now to Mr. Martic. This is the moment for you. You remember we had another Status Conference just four months ago. It is the moment for you now to tell to the Court what could be your problems. Do you have any special issues you would like to present just now? And also, what about your health, your situation in the prison? Do you have any problems you would like to inform the Court about, their existence?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As far as the conditions of detention are concerned, I have nothing to complain about. I think that the conditions are correct. The treatment of the officials and the warden there are most proper. The only complaint I have pertains to the proceedings. I believe that there are some things that are not necessary when bringing indictees here. You know that we are subjected to a search, body search, and that's fine, but what I don't understand is that after we're finished here and when we return back, the body search is carried out once again, and I don't see any need for that. Is there anything you can do about that? This is one particular complaint that I have. I think it is quite unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Well, thank you for telling me, but I don't think I can do much about that. Anyway, I will try, but I am logically informed that whenever you have to get out or go back to the Detention Unit some searches have to be performed. So I am sorry, but I don't think you can be dispensed with that. I am glad to learn that your health condition is good and that you don't have any special complaints other than the ones that you had submitted to this Court. So please sit down. And nothing else is --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: I see that Mr. Milovancevic would like to say something. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, Your Honour, in addition to what I said about our progress we have achieved so far in our contacts with the Prosecution, I wanted to say a few things concerning the methods of payment. The Defence right now is faced with something that could grow into a serious problem. As Defence counsel, I had a duty to study the Rules, because we have both oral and written contacts with the Registry, and I have to say that the bills are reduced in such a way that could potentially present a problem for the Defence in the future. So far, I have avoided to trouble the Chamber with written submissions, knowing how busy the Trial Chamber is, and I wish to express hope that these problems will be resolved in the future and will not deteriorate. We have a very serious task before us, a very responsible task, and we are doing our best to carry out our duties in the best possible way. However, we believe that the Registry, with all due respect to their duty to verify all the invoices and so on, so despite of that, we believe that the Registry should have in its mind that the Defence here is doing a very serious job. That's all I have to say. I hope that this will be resolved. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MARTIN-CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milovancevic. As you know, these problems are chiefly related with the action of the Registry, but nevertheless, if it could be so complicated as to impair the possibility of fairness in dealing with this case, the Chamber will take also care of that. I hope that you have been already said not to -- well, that is something that has been advised to you to do, is just to try to manage within the limitations, and I hope you are aware of that and you are behaving in relation with that. But that is the most I can tell you for the time being. Okay. If nothing else is going to be suggested, I am going to adjourn this meeting, not without thanking you all for coming, thanking the Registry also, and last but not least to the translators. So the meeting is adjourned.
